title: Cutting work and school to hear Freddie Keppard at the Clark Hotel
summary: In 1915 he skipped work and school to hear the Original Creole Orchestra and Keppard, and listened to them practise at the Clark Hotel.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah. "In 1915, the Pantages (unintelligible) Freddie Keppard and Hayes's (phonetic) Theater brought Freddy Cabbot (phonetic) and the Original Creole Orchestra to Los Angeles.
It says here that that was during the time that you were still at Bullard (phonetic), and going to school, and you cut both of them to hear the band every single day at Pantages Theater.
I stayed out, cut the work, cut the school to stay out there and listen to that band.
Yeah, I (unintelligible) liked the-- Freddy Keppard (phonetic)--what's his name, Keppard?

Yeah, I liked to hear him play. And then, in the daytime I'd duck school and everyplace else, and I'd go down to his house. He lived right there on--oh, shu'--just give me a minute, I'm gonna' get this, Baby--I've got to get it, cause he was one of my best ones. Listening. I could listen real good at him. Freddie Keppard. Freddy Keppard. And, you know that thing--
(inaudible) That's all right. Don't worry about this.
You know where the place was on Central?
That's it. That's where I used to go, up there and listen to them guys play. They practiced, and practiced there, every day.
There was a ballroom there, wasn't there, on that corner?
Yeah. Would practice there every day.
So you got a chance to meet some of the musicians?
Where were they from? Do you know?
I'm sorry that I had to do all them things. See Suzie will think I'm nutty. I know what I did.
